name: release-notes
title: Release notes
summary: Writes the release notes for a range of commits by running the scripts your team already had, unchanged.
blurb: Most teams have twenty crusty shell and Python scripts nobody wants to port, and every agent framework asks them to port them. heddle does not: a tool is a program that reads JSON on stdin and prints JSON on stdout, so the distance between a script you already run by hand and a tool an agent can call is about fifteen lines. This entry is that claim, made concrete. scripts/ holds three plainly pre-agent programs — flags in, text out, non-zero on failure, written for a person — and they are not touched, not imported and not rewritten; they still work by hand. tools/ holds one shim per script: read the JSON, spend it as flags, run the thing, print one JSON object. When a script fails, its own exit code and its own stderr come back verbatim, because a friendlier error invented by the shim is the one thing the person debugging cannot use. The agent on top reads what the scripts print and writes notes grouped the way a reader would group them, with a rule it is held to: every line must trace to a commit it was shown, and a subject it cannot interpret goes in an "unclear" list by hash rather than being guessed at. Swap the three scripts for your own twenty and the shape does not change.
